chains.title: Null: no TF-mediated effect of rs56007086; linked causal variant or no allelic effect
predictions: No allele-specific TF binding at rs56007086
No reproducible ref/alt enhancer reporter difference in MCF7
Any TOX3/16q12 expression association is due to a linked causal variant or is not allele-specific at this position
falsified_if: Allele-specific FOXA1 binding is reproducibly ref>alt in MCF7 nuclear extract and is abolished by FOXA1 knockdown or anti-FOXA1 supershift.
Ref/alt enhancer reporter activity differs in MCF7 in a FOXA1-dependent manner.
The locus shows an allele-specific chromatin/expression effect that tracks with the variant rather than a linked variant.

chains.title: FOXA1 binds the ref allele at a 16q12 enhancer and modulates TOX3

links.claim: FOXA1 binds the ref G allele more strongly than the alt A allele at rs56007086.
rs56007086 lies in a 16q12.1 enhancer element near TOX3/CASC16 whose activity can be modulated by FOXA1.
This enhancer regulates TOX3 expression in breast cells.
The relevant cell type is MCF7 breast luminal epithelial cells, where FOXA1 is expressed and active.
Altered FOXA1-dependent enhancer activity changes TOX3 expression and thereby influences 16q12 breast cancer risk; the net direction is not assumed because FOXA1 can repress.

predictions: FOXA1 knockdown reduces allele-specific enhancer/reporter effect
FOXA1 ChIP enrichment at the locus is allele-biased toward ref
Effect should be FOXA1-dependent and detectable in MCF7
falsified_if: Ref and alt probes show equal FOXA1 binding in EMSA or allele-specific ChIP
FOXA1 knockdown does not change ref/alt reporter activity in MCF7
Allele-specific enhancer activity is not present at rs56007086

chains.title: ESR1/ER binds the ref allele at an estrogen-responsive 16q12 enhancer

links.claim: ESR1/ER binds the ref G allele more strongly than the alt A allele at rs56007086.
rs56007086 lies in an estrogen-responsive 16q12.1 enhancer near TOX3/CASC16.
This estrogen-responsive enhancer regulates TOX3 expression.
The relevant context is MCF7 breast luminal epithelial cells with estrogen-receptor signaling.
Altered ESR1-dependent enhancer activity changes TOX3 expression and influences breast cancer risk in an estrogen-dependent manner.

predictions: Effect is enhanced by estrogen and reduced by ESR1 knockdown
FOXA1 knockdown should not fully abolish the ESR1-dependent allele effect
ERE mutation should reduce reporter effect
falsified_if: Allele-specific ESR1/ER binding is not seen after estrogen treatment
ESR1 knockdown or ERE mutation does not affect ref/alt reporter activity
FOXA1, not ESR1, accounts for the allele-specific binding

chains.title: CEBPB binds the ref allele at a 16q12 enhancer

links.claim: CEBPB binds the ref G allele more strongly than the alt A allele at rs56007086.
rs56007086 lies in a 16q12.1 enhancer near TOX3/CASC16 with a CEBPB-responsive element.
The relevant cell type is MCF7 breast luminal epithelial cells, where CEBPB can contribute to enhancer activity.
Altered CEBPB-dependent enhancer activity changes TOX3 expression and influences breast cancer risk.

predictions: CEBPB knockdown reduces ref/alt reporter difference
CEBPB ChIP enrichment at the locus is allele-biased toward ref
Effect is independent of FOXA1 and ESR1
falsified_if: Allele-specific CEBPB binding is absent in MCF7 nuclear extract
CEBPB knockdown does not affect ref/alt reporter activity
The allele effect is explained by FOXA1 or ESR1

matrix.test: Allele-specific FOXA1 EMSA with MCF7 nuclear extract plus anti-FOXA1 supershift

outcomes.outcome: Ref>alt FOXA1 binding and anti-FOXA1 supershift
No allele-specific FOXA1 binding or supershift

matrix.test: Allele-specific EMSA with anti-ESR1 and anti-CEBPB supershifts

next_experiment: Allele-specific EMSA/supershift at rs56007086 using MCF7 nuclear extract and anti-FOXA1 antibody, comparing ref G and alt A probes; this is the cheapest direct test separating the top FOXA1 chain from the null. A positive ref>alt FOXA1 supershift supports the FOXA1 chain; absence supports the null or shifts weight to another TF chain.
